newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, gasoline and fuel oil slip.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, gasoline and fuel oil slip.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Tuesday, but gasoline was the weakest, ignoring crude's substantial rally.
Premium unleaded gasoline cargoes fell about $4 to $223/$224 cif as ample supply of lower octane grades dragged the market lower, traders said.
Demand for premium unleaded was seen in Turkey and for leaded and unleaded in Italy in December.
Naphtha rose $1 after a Med refiner bought a 25,000-tonne Libyan cargo and traders saw a poor weather forecast at Skikda.
"I think the market is basically balanced with no rush to get prompt supplies and no cargoes around," an Italian trader said.
Gas oil firmed $2.25 on IPE futures and premiums were stable to slightly weaker, trader said.

Traders reported ample demand and supply for heating oil, but said the market was deadlocked while players waited for the results of a Turkish tender for four carges of 25,000 tonnes each of 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil for December. Responses are due by Wednesday.
"No one wants to move. Sellers don't want to come off their prices until they see what happens to Turkey. The buyers are convinced it has to come off so they don't want to pay up," one trader said.
In low sulphur diesel, two Algerians were offered loading 18-22 and 20-30 and a small parcel was offered out of Malta.

Fuel oil slipped in line with the weaker sentiment in the north, but many traders were predicting more gains soon. Portugal was seen well covered by hydro-electric demand, but one trader expected Turkey to tender to buy cracked fuel soon.
